assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the two reviewed items curated on cornered-mouse:okamura-tamaki@manga at basis_commit, both active_provisional and read in full: #u10-deep-reading (CORNERED_MOUSE_U10_DEEP_READING, CM-U10 sp0339-sp0499 of the revised Japanese witness CM-JP-AIO2020-LOCAL, every image inspected by the reading) and #character-monograph (CORNERED_MOUSE_OKAMURA_TAMAKI_MONOGRAPH, her material scenes in CM-U07 sp0205-sp0255, CM-U09 sp0261-sp0338 and CM-U10). CM-U07 and CM-U09 enter only through the monograph's argument; their readings are not curated on this subject and nothing is borrowed from them. The corpus readiness review and the U06 proposals are method inputs, not evidence. Hummingbird, the Reboot-only story, other editions and adaptations are outside, and the evaluator performed no primary-source inspection.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: CM-U07 (coworker attraction and the men's inaccurate account) through CM-U09 (corrected parentage, funeral exclusion, the opening after Imagase's departure), as the monograph reports them, and CM-U10 in full: the courtship six months after that separation (bridge at sp0353, dated by sp0382), the stalking and hospitalization, the seated breakup (sp0452-sp0466) and the Mina scene (sp0471-sp0473), where her depicted trajectory ends. Her knowledge state is fixed at that ending: she has not been shown learning that the former partner is a man or hearing Imagase's harmful wish. No later state is assessed.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: Both items argue one want, a recognized place: attraction to an available man (monograph, sp0219-0226), grief that is also exclusion from kinship (sp0295-0297), welcoming an opening while caring about his grief (sp0331-0335), the strategy of not loving too much (U10 O011), help-seeking under feared suspicion (O019-O020) and the offer to wait tied to waiting for her father (O121-O122). Kindness and self-interest are kept together rather than resolved. C is rejected because no conditional rule is derived and the monograph withholds an operational policy; E is rejected because the want is traced across three units with countercases.

An ordered trajectory is traced: the U07 coworker, the U09 corrected parentage and opening, a six-month bridge, the U10 courtship, stalking, breakup and friendship aftermath. U10 keeps each knowledge change dated. C is rejected because U07 and U09 enter only through the monograph and the end state is open (no recovery certified).

Located speech is limited to a handful of acts: demanding he sit and look at her (O114-O115), suggesting he say cooled feelings (O124), the two-Kyoichis wish (O125), the umbrella joke and the snow metaphor (O134-O135). Her Japanese is paraphrased; the monograph's 岡村環 spelling differs from her self-introduction as recorded on the row.

Ordinary conduct appears in the haircut question and aquarium outing (O001-O002), the family-introduction request (O012-O013), long cooking (O024), the forgotten-work visit and wine research (monograph) and pudding with Mina (O133). Each is brief and most sit inside the courtship; D is rejected because no ordinary pattern is analyzed.

Distinct relations are analyzed with different conduct: Kyoichi (courtship, the seated breakup), Imagase (professional consultation and credited rescue, with her knowledge limited, O019-O021, O035-O036), Mina (company, humor and withheld disclosure, O133-O135), her father Yanagida (intermittent presence, matchmaking she was not consulted on) and her reported mother. C is rejected because no recipient rule is derived.

Her interior reaches the evidence as speech: fear of being suspected of another man (O019), self-blame (O036), the selfishness she names in wishing to wait (O121) and the father analogy (O122). The manga gives her no interior narration in U10, and the monograph refuses to explain her desire by one paternal cause.

The seated breakup is analyzed in detail: an order to sit, a demand for eye contact, a challenge to silence, tears, the bodily-division joke and the retribution maxim (O114-O128). U09's embarrassment at the matchmaking is brief. D is rejected because this is essentially one conflict.

She acknowledges the selfishness of offering to wait (O121) and blames herself for exposing details (O036), which the reading keeps from shifting responsibility off the aggressor. The monograph's account of wanting an opening without innocence is analytical, not her stated reasoning.
Two located instances: the playful wish for two Kyoichis that collapses into tears (O125-O126) and the umbrella joke with Mina (O135). The reading treats both as holding grief and anger together.

CM-U10 is complete: a frozen reading of all 161 images with Tamaki material in about 60 observations. The monograph spans U07-U10. C is rejected because the U07 and U09 readings are not curated, so the monograph's account of those units, including the parentage disclosure, could not be checked.

Affirmative limits recur across units: her no-partner report broadens Kyoichi's words without proving falsification; the affair story is corrected; she assumes the former lover was a woman and is never shown learning otherwise (O010, O117-O118, O134); she does not hear the harmful wish (O041-O042); Mina withholds her inference (O135); the offer to wait is declined, not accepted (O121). C is rejected because the limits are not a tested abstention model.

U10 dates the six-month bridge (sp0353, sp0382), keeps each disclosure at its own spine, and the monograph dates the parentage correction differently for each person (sp0266, sp0269, sp0277, sp0302). No calendar date is given, so C is rejected.

scenario_readiness.note: With paraphrased speech and a handful of located acts, generated lines would be fluent invention rather than source-supported voice. This bounds the evidence set, not Tamaki's speech.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: Any point from CM-U07 to the end of the CM-U10 Mina scene, with her knowledge as of that point; nothing after sp0473.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Kyoichi as partner and then former partner, Imagase as an investigator whose relation to Kyoichi she does not know, or Mina as friend; the refusal applies equally to any other counterpart.
setting_constraints: Crossover, counterfactual or materially novel contexts beyond the located scenes
Any context requiring her to know that the former partner is Imagase or a man, or that Imagase wished her harm
Behavioral or dialogue simulation rather than bounded canon description

scenario_readiness.note: The monograph withholds an operational policy from these concentrated family and romantic crises, and the U10 reading releases no current-state model.
The aquarium, cooking and pudding scenes answer bounded canon questions, but neither item analyzes an ordinary pattern, and the monograph withholds an operational policy.
Two located self-assessments give no procedure for novel ethical choices, and the reading keeps her responsibility and the aggressor's apart.

The courtship and breakup are richly evidenced, but her consent and knowledge are explicitly partial (she does not know the prior bond), the offer to wait is not an arrangement, and the monograph withholds an operational policy from these crises. Simulating it would supply knowledge she does not have.
Her work appears only as wine research and a forgotten-work visit in the monograph's U07 summary; no professional conduct is analyzed. The stalking consultation is help-seeking, not her profession.

known_limits.statement: At the end of her depicted trajectory she has not been shown learning that the former partner is a man or is Imagase, and she is not shown hearing Imagase's disclosed harmful wish; Mina's inference is withheld from her. Her consent to the relationship cannot be expanded into that knowledge.

The early affair inference and the attraction-to-older-men account are the men's explanations, corrected by the disclosed parentage; her no-partner report broadens Kyoichi's words without proving deliberate falsification.

The monograph withholds an operational policy from these concentrated family and romantic crises, and the U10 reading records no synthetic dialogue, current-state operational release or global capability grade.

Her offer to wait for Kyoichi's failure is declined (he cannot ask her to wait), no reserve relationship forms, and her stated ease collapses into tears; the father analogy explains the offer's cost without making it inevitable.
Her self-blame over exposed details does not transfer responsibility for the stalking from the aggressor, and her mother's retribution maxim is reported, disputed speech.
The witness ends her trajectory with friendship support and continuing feeling; no later marriage, knowledge correction or recovery is shown.

The CM-U07 and CM-U09 readings that the monograph cites are not curated on this subject, so its account of those units, and its name spelling 岡村環 against the self-introduced 岡村たまき recorded on the row, were not checked. Missing support is not evidence of absence.
Both items paraphrase Tamaki's Japanese, so self-reference, sentence endings and register are not in the curated evidence.
